title: Evaluating Generate–Validate–Repair Pipelines for Intent‑to‑Configuration NetOps Tasks: A Preregistered Paired Study
abstract: We preregistered and executed a paired confirmatory study that isolates downstream validator and repair effects under shared_initial_candidate semantics. Using a 1,000‑task synthetic NetOps stress corpus (2,000 paired episodes) and a deterministic digital‑twin validator, we compared a baseline single‑shot generator to a guarded generate→validate→repair pipeline with a canary stage. Declared model: gpt‑5‑mini (provider: openai_responses). Under the preregistered design (exactly one sampled initial generation per pair reused by both arms; guarded allowed at most one repair call), observed outcomes were: baseline safe‑deploy = 995/1000 = 0.995; guarded safe‑deploy = 1000/1000 = 1.000; paired difference = 0.005 (n11=995, n10=5, n01=0, n00=0). Preregistered primary test (exact two‑sided McNemar) yields p = 0.0625 (not < 0.05). The preregistered paired bootstrap percentile 95% CI (10,000 resamples, seed = 1729) is [0.001, 0.01] and is presented as a descriptive summary. Only five validator‑triggered repairs occurred and total hosted model calls used = 1005 (shared_initial = 1000; repair = 5). We report the exact McNemar as the confirmatory outcome, label any one‑sided tests exploratory (one‑sided McNemar p = 0.03125, post‑hoc), and interpret the small absolute guarded benefit in light of sparse discordant counts, extremely high baseline validity, and the constraints imposed by shared_initial_candidate semantics.

sections.introduction:
Automating intent→configuration translation promises operational efficiency for network operations (NetOps) but introduces safety risks: multi‑step sequencing errors, transient invariant violations, and protected‑field interference can turn plausible command sequences into harmful actions. Prior surveys and controlled studies document LLM hallucination, prompt sensitivity, and structured‑output failures that degrade correctness for code and configuration generation, motivating architectures that pair generative models with deterministic validators and bounded repair procedures (generate→validate→repair) [1],[2].

This work reports a preregistered, artifact‑grounded paired experiment (cand‑003‑stud‑001) that intentionally isolates downstream validation and a single permitted repair by using shared_initial_candidate generation semantics: baseline and guarded episodes begin from the exact same sampled initial candidate and differ only in deterministic validator decision and the guarded path's at‑most‑one repair call. Our research question is therefore precise: when baseline and guarded conditions reuse the same initial sampled candidate, to what degree can downstream deterministic validation plus a single repair call (guarded pipeline with canary) improve paired safe‑deploy outcomes versus reusing the same candidate unmodified (baseline)?

Contributions. (1) A preregistered paired experiment (Npairs = 1000) with deterministic task selection from the challenging_workflow_stress_v1 corpus and archived validator traces. (2) Full, artifact‑grounded execution accounting and exact confirmatory inference following the frozen analysis plan (exact two‑sided McNemar; paired bootstrap CI as preregistered descriptive summary). (3) A focused interpretation that (a) clarifies the inferential primacy of the preregistered two‑sided McNemar test, (b) explains why a bootstrap CI can exclude zero under extremely sparse discordant counts, and (c) highlights the epistemic limits introduced by shared_initial_candidate semantics, the synthetic corpus, and single‑model scope.
sections.related_work:
Empirical and survey literature documents two relevant empirical axes. First, LLMs produce structured outputs with frequent syntactic and semantic failure modes: hallucinations, prompt sensitivity, and code/configuration generation errors have been repeatedly observed across domains [2],[7]. Second, system and benchmark work in NetOps and agentic AI advocate pairing generative models with deterministic validators, constrained decoding, and governance layers (proof‑carrying traces, protocol‑mediated execution) to reduce automation risk and to create auditable execution evidence [4],[5],[6]. Constrained decoding and schema‑aware planning reduce syntactic/executable errors in structured domains, though much evidence comes from other domains and relies on validator/tool fidelity when applied to networking [3].

Our study complements this body of work by preregistering a paired estimand that isolates downstream validate/repair effects when the initial candidate is held constant. This avoids conflating validator/repair benefits with improvements that would arise from alternative prompt templates, constrained decoding methods, or independent sampling of multiple first‑pass generations—interventions that were not executed under the frozen preregistration and therefore lie outside this estimand.
sections.methodology:
Preregistration and confirmatory design. The experiment preregistration cand‑003‑stud‑001 was frozen prior to any model calls; preregistration SHA‑256 archived in the execution manifest = ab4c6436c6ece56bf47da7730d50485a17cdb9bb86a90a4231042303d3b489ec. Design: paired binary confirmatory design with task_count = 1000 deterministically sampled from the challenging_workflow_stress_v1 synthetic corpus; generation_semantics = shared_initial_candidate (exactly one initial generation per task reused by both arms); initial_generation_calls_per_task = 1; maximum_repair_calls_per_task = 1; primary estimand = paired_success_rate_difference_guarded_minus_baseline; primary test = exact two‑sided McNemar. The preregistration specified a paired bootstrap percentile 95% CI (10,000 resamples, bootstrap_seed = 1729) as a descriptive secondary summary and prespecified missingness treatments and multiplicity rules.

Execution primitives and validator. Declared model/provider: gpt‑5‑mini (provider: openai_responses). Orchestration framework: hosted_netops_gvr_v1. Deterministic validator/digital twin: deterministic_netops_validator_v5 (validator_version = 5.0). The validator enforces manifest constraints including required sequence ordering, allowed_touched_fields, protected interfaces, and other workflow policies; it emits a deterministic binary safe‑deploy verdict and structured validator traces archived per episode. The archived execution/model_configuration.json records temperature = null/unset; we explicitly state null/unset is not evidence of deterministic hosted‑model sampling and does not imply temperature = 0.

Task corpus and deterministic sampling. Tasks are synthetic NetOps maintenance/change intents, each accompanied by an initial_state, expected_final_state, required_sequence, allowed_touched_fields, and difficulty label (very_hard or extreme). Task selection followed the preregistered deterministic ordinal rule to produce exactly 1000 unique task indices. The validator's acceptance criterion for a candidate is the preregistered scoring_rule 'full_intent_constraint_validation', which yields the binary outcome used in the paired analysis.

Shared_initial_candidate semantics: interpretive consequences. Because generation_semantics = shared_initial_candidate, both the baseline and guarded episodes begin from the same sampled initial candidate; the guarded arm may reject the candidate and invoke at most one allowed repair call. Under this semantics, any observed paired difference can arise only from deterministic validation decisions and permitted repair(s) — not from first‑pass generation differences, alternative prompts, or constrained decoding arms that were not executed. This restriction is central to the estimand and is reported explicitly so readers do not extrapolate the results to interventions that were not part of the frozen experiment.

Execution accounting and failure treatment. The preregistration limited retries (maximum_attempts_per_call = 1) and prespecified missingness handling; the adapter/executor recorded completed_episode_count = 2000, failed_episode_count = 0, and provider audit counts. The analysis executor applied the preregistered 'complete_pair_primary' rule for missingness; sensitivity analyses treating failures as unsafe were preregistered and archived but not invoked because no failed episodes occurred.
sections.results:
Execution and accounting (artifact‑grounded). The run began 2026‑09‑01T06:31:07Z and completed 2026‑09‑01T08:38:57Z. Planned episodes = 2000; completed = 2000; complete_pairs = 1000; failed episodes = 0. Provider audit (deterministic_reconciliation.json) records hosted_model_call_event_count = 1005, stage_counts = {shared_initial_generation = 1000, repair = 5}, and cross_condition_cache_key_reuse_observed = false; total model calls used = 1005.

Primary paired outcomes and preregistered inferential test. The 2×2 paired contingency table (analysis/paired_contingency_table.csv) is: n11 = 995 (both succeeded), n10 = 5 (guarded succeeded, baseline failed), n01 = 0 (baseline succeeded, guarded failed), n00 = 0 (both failed). Observed success rates: baseline = 995/1000 = 0.995; guarded = 1000/1000 = 1.000; observed paired difference (guarded − baseline) = 0.005. The preregistered primary confirmatory test (exact two‑sided McNemar) returns p = 0.0625; this does not meet the preregistered two‑sided α = 0.05 threshold and thus H1 is not supported by the preregistered confirmatory inference.

Paired bootstrap descriptive summary and exploratory checks. The preregistered paired bootstrap percentile 95% CI (10,000 resamples, seed = 1729) yields [0.001, 0.01] (artifact: analysis/analysis_log.jsonl). We emphasize this interval was registered as a descriptive summary only; it can exclude zero in regimes with extremely sparse discordant counts because bootstrap resampling over 1,000 paired observations with only five discordant events produces percentile bounds sensitive to the discreteness and resampling scheme. A one‑sided McNemar (guarded > baseline) computed post‑hoc yields p = 0.03125; this directionally one‑sided test was not prespecified in cand‑003‑stud‑001 and is therefore reported as exploratory/post‑hoc and does not alter the preregistered confirmatory conclusion.

Repair mechanics and representative traces. Only five validator‑triggered repairs occurred (repair stage_count = 5). Representative archived episode artifacts (execution/scoring/*.json) show the validator rejecting initial candidates due to required_sequence or protected_field violations and the adapter invoking the single allowed repair call; the repaired candidate was then accepted by the validator. All raw responses, provider call traces, repair traces (where present), and validator traces are archived and referenced in the execution manifest and deterministic_reconciliation.json.

Contamination, exclusions, and missingness. Preregistered contamination checks and exclusion rules found no prompt‑leakage flags and no deterministic emulator errors; contamination_summary.csv is empty and missingness_summary.csv records zero failed or unscorable episodes. No post‑hoc exclusions were applied; all seeds and deterministic sampling rules were fixed per preregistration.
sections.discussion:
Inferential hierarchy and interpretation. The preregistered exact two‑sided McNemar test is the study's confirmatory inference and did not reach α = 0.05 (p = 0.0625). Secondary descriptive summaries (paired bootstrap CI) and any post‑hoc one‑sided tests are explicitly secondary or exploratory: the bootstrap CI was preregistered as descriptive and the one‑sided McNemar was not prespecified. Presenting the confirmatory null together with descriptive summaries is faithful to the preregistered analysis plan but risks misinterpretation; we therefore restate the inferential priority: the exact two‑sided McNemar result governs confirmatory claims.

Why a bootstrap CI can exclude zero while the exact McNemar is not significant. With extremely sparse discordant counts (n10 + n01 = 5), the exact McNemar test's discrete null distribution yields a two‑sided p = 0.0625 boundary for the observed ordering (n10 = 5, n01 = 0). Bootstrap resampling of paired outcomes—especially percentile intervals—can produce nonzero lower bounds because resamples that pick discordant events at different multiplicities shift the sample proportion distribution; percentile‑based bounds therefore reflect the resampling distribution's sensitivity to rare-event variability rather than overturning an exact discrete paired test. This nuance explains the apparent discrepancy and underscores why the preregistered exact McNemar result remains the primary inferential statement.

Mechanistic reading within shared_initial_candidate semantics. Because both conditions reuse the same initial candidates, observed paired improvements can only follow from deterministic validator decisions and permitted repairs. The five observed repairs illustrate that a deterministic validator with sufficient rule coverage can correct some ordering/sequence violations. However, the low repair count may reflect (a) high initial candidate validity for the chosen model/prompt in the synthetic corpus, (b) validator acceptances for many semantic classes, or (c) validator rule‑set limits that do not flag certain semantic errors. Distinguishing these mechanisms requires follow‑ups that vary generator semantics, repair budget, and validator rule sets.

Threats to validity and generalizability. Construct validity: the binary safe‑deploy outcome depends on deterministic_netops_validator_v5's rule coverage; omitted checks would inflate apparent success. Internal validity: shared_initial_candidate semantics isolate downstream effects but preclude measuring prompt/decoding interventions. External validity: the synthetic corpus and single‑model scope (gpt‑5‑mini) limit generalization to heterogeneous production environments and other model families. Conclusion validity: near‑unity baseline success yields sparse discordant pairs, reducing sensitivity for exact paired tests and making small absolute differences difficult to detect with the preregistered power assumption (the preregistered power plan assumed a much lower baseline ≈ 0.60). These limitations are reported explicitly in the archived preregistration and manifest.
sections.conclusion: In this preregistered paired study on a 1,000‑task synthetic NetOps stress corpus with shared_initial_candidate semantics, a guarded generate→validate→repair pipeline produced a small absolute paired improvement (0.005) relative to a baseline single‑shot generator; the preregistered exact two‑sided McNemar test did not reach α = 0.05 (p = 0.0625). Only five validator repairs were invoked and total model calls used = 1005. The confirmatory inference follows the preregistered exact McNemar result; any one‑sided McNemar outcome is exploratory and was not prespecified. Artifact‑grounded evidence indicates verifier‑guided repair can avert some unsafe outcomes in synthetic workflow settings, but measurable marginal gains depend critically on baseline failure prevalence, validator sensitivity/coverage, and permitted repair budget. We recommend preregistered follow‑ups that (a) evaluate independent first‑pass generation arms (no shared_initial_candidate) to measure prompt/decoding interventions, (b) sweep repair budgets to quantify marginal returns per failure class, (c) expand validator rule suites and topology heterogeneity, and (d) include multiple model families. All artifacts referenced in this paper (preregistration, execution manifests, raw outputs, validator traces, and analysis artifacts) are archived with the run to support reproducibility and follow‑up preregistered experiments.

limitations: Single‑model scope: only the declared model gpt‑5‑mini was evaluated; results do not generalize across model families or versions.

Synthetic corpus and deterministic validator: tasks come from a synthetic stress corpus and validation used a deterministic digital twin (deterministic_netops_validator_v5); external validity to heterogeneous vendor/legacy environments is limited.

Shared_initial_candidate semantics: the paired comparison isolates downstream validator/repair effects only; it does not measure differences that would arise from independent first‑pass generations or alternative prompting arms that were not executed (those arms were not part of the frozen preregistration).

Low baseline failure prevalence: baseline success = 99.5%; the preregistered power plan assumed baseline≈0.60 and a target effect of 0.15, so the observed baseline greatly reduces sensitivity to detect small absolute gains. This mismatch is reported explicitly and reduces the study's ability to detect very small practical effects using the preregistered confirmatory test.
Sparse repairs and interpretation limits: only five validator repairs were invoked, constraining inference about repair efficacy across failure modes.

Statistical nuance: the preregistered primary test is exact two‑sided McNemar (p = 0.0625). The paired bootstrap percentile CI [0.001, 0.01] is a preregistered descriptive summary but is sensitive to sparse discordant counts; a one‑sided McNemar (p = 0.03125) was computed post‑hoc and is explicitly labeled exploratory because it was not prespecified in the frozen preregistration.

Construct validity: the safe‑deploy binary depends on the emulator/validator's rule set; semantic and emergent multi‑device policy violations may be underrepresented in the validator's modeled constraints.
